Thanks for the demo earlier, Sean — the team and I appreciate the speed and the observability features. A couple of quick clarifying questions as we scope an internal pilot: 

1) For our use case (real-time assistant inside our analytics dashboard), we care a lot about predictable p99 latency under bursty traffic. From your comments, I think Hosted could work if rate limits and endpoints are suitable — can you confirm what Hosted pilot rate limits look like?

2) What signals push you to recommend Dedicated versus Hosted for an initial pilot? Our peak concurrent users are likely to be ~120 active sessions during business hours; average session generates ~400 tokens per minute but bursts to 2k tokens on some requests.

3) We have HIPAA-adjacent customers — curious if Hosted has VPC/on-prem prerequisites for any compliance checks, or if Private deployment is only for later-stage production.

Claire — great to hear and thanks for the concise list. See answers inline below and next steps at the end. I’ve attached a short hosted quickstart checklist and a traffic template for Tom to fill.

1) Hosted pilot rate limits / endpoints:
- For Hosted pilot accounts we typically provision 2 dedicated endpoints (staging + pilot) with adjustable ratecaps. Default pilot ratecap is 60 requests/sec across the pilot endpoint, burstable to 120rps for short periods depending on model and token rate.
- Per-token concurrency and p99 latency depend on model selection (we recommended a medium-sized open model during the demo). We can surface a per-endpoint SLO for the pilot window if you provide a 48h traffic sample (use the attached template).

2) Signals for recommending Dedicated vs Hosted:
- Recommend Dedicated when: sustained high throughput (1000+ rps or consistent GPU utilization > 70%), hard throughput SLAs, or strict data isolation needs.
- Hosted is a good fit for: pilots, variable traffic, and teams that prefer faster onboarding and less infra ops. Given your current estimate (120 active sessions, bursts up to 2k tokens), Hosted pilot makes sense as the first step — we’ll monitor and if your 48h sample shows sustained high concurrency, we can propose a Dedicated sizing plan.

3) Compliance / VPC considerations:
- Hosted supports encrypted-in-transit and at-rest by default; for regulated workloads (HIPAA-like) we often recommend Private (VPC or on-prem) for final production, but Hosted can be used for initial evaluation if you don’t plan to send PHI during the pilot.

Next steps:
- Tom: please complete the attached traffic_profile_template.xlsx and return within 3 business days.
- Claire: approve a pilot window (we recommend 2 weeks) and confirm the model family you want to test.
- Jonas: can you confirm the estimated pilot SLO and any recommended endpoint throttles for FinLytics?

Attachments: hosted-quickstart-checklist.pdf, traffic-profile-template.xlsx

Best,

Claire / Sean — adding some technical detail to help Tom scope the traffic profile and for the pilot SLO. Apologies for the long note.

Pilot endpoint sizing guidance (hosted):
- If you choose the medium open model we demoed, expect typical per-request processing of ~45–120ms per token on our hosted fleet at 128-token generations; p99 will depend heavily on KV cache hit rate and sequence lengths.
- For your burst patterns (2k tokens occasional): plan for temporary throttling on single requests. We can offer a burst policy that queues requests up to 10s before returning a 429 if concurrency exceeds the pilot threshold.

Rate limits and throttling knobs:
- Two main knobs: requests/sec per endpoint and concurrent inference slots. For the pilot we usually set RPS=60, concurrent_slots=40. If your traffic profile shows sustained concurrency >40 across the pilot window, we should move to Dedicated.

Fallbacks & graceful degradation:
- We can configure model-variant fallback to a smaller/cheaper model under heavy load to keep the app responsive (e.g., reduce token budget / switch to a faster quantized variant).

Security notes:
- Hosted audit logs (request metadata, timestamps) can be exported daily for compliance review. For PHI/PHI-adjacent data we recommend either anonymizing data in the pilot or using Private for production to maintain strict controls.

Suggested pilot SLO for FinLytics:
- Target median latency < 300ms for typical 400-token requests, p95 < 800ms during normal hours. Allow p99 up to 2.5s during rare bursts with fallback enabled.

I can provision the pilot endpoints as soon as we have the traffic template. Happy to jump on a 20-min call with Tom to walk through the template.

Cheers,
